Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 28.1.0 to 30.0.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.0.1

  • Fixed getComputedStyle() with calc() and other functions throwing an exception, which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Sped up up range operations on large documents (@​leonidaz)

v30.0.0

Breaking changes:

  • Node.js minimum version raised to ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0.

Other changes:

  • Added CSS.escape() and CSS.supports() functions. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Added 'background-position-x' and 'background-position-y' CSS properties. (@​olagokemills)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to convert length values into pixels. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed CSS function serialization, e.g., in the return value of getPropertyValue(). (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed the type of error thrown by document.evaluate() (@​dokson)

v29.1.1

  • Fixed 'border-radius' computed style serialization. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed computed style computation when using 'background-origin' and 'background-clip' CSS properties. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Significantly optimized initial calls to getComputedStyle(), before the cache warms up. (@​asamuzaK)

v29.1.0

  • Added basic support for the ratio CSS type. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() sometimes returning outdated results after CSS was modified. (@​asamuzaK)

v29.0.2

  • Significantly improved and sped up getComputedStyle(). Computed value rules are now applied across a broader set of properties, and include fixes related to inheritance, defaulting keywords, custom properties, and color-related values such as currentcolor and system colors. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed CSS 'background' and 'border' shorthand parsing. (@​asamuzaK)

v29.0.1

  • Fixed CSS parsing of 'border', 'background', and their sub-shorthands containing keywords or var(). (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to return a more functional CSSStyleDeclaration object, including indexed access support, which regressed in v29.0.0.

v29.0.0

Breaking changes:

  • Node.js v22.13.0+ is now the minimum supported v22 version (was v22.12.0+).

Other changes:

  • Overhauled the CSSOM implementation, replacing the @acemir/cssom and cssstyle dependencies with fresh internal implementations built on webidl2js wrappers and the css-tree parser. Serialization, parsing, and API behavior is improved in various ways, especially around edge cases.
  • Added CSSCounterStyleRule and CSSNamespaceRule to jsdom Windows.
  • Added cssMediaRule.matches and cssSupportsRule.matches getters.
  • Added proper media query parsing in MediaList, using css-tree instead of naive comma-splitting. Invalid queries become "not all" per spec.
  • Added cssKeyframeRule.keyText getter/setter validation.
  • Added cssStyleRule.selectorText setter validation: invalid selectors are now rejected.
  • Added styleSheet.ownerNode, styleSheet.href, and styleSheet.title.
  • Added bad port blocking per the fetch specification, preventing fetches to commonly-abused ports.
  • Improved Document initialization performance by lazily initializing the CSS selector engine, avoiding ~0.5 ms of overhead per Document. (@​thypon)

pullRequests.body:
Updates the existing `@wensity` entry in `apps/v4/registry/directory.json`. Three fields on one object; no other entries are touched.

### What changed

| Field | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `.../ksparth12/wensity-shadcn-registry/main/{name}.json` | `.../wensity/registry/main/{name}.json` |
| `homepage` | `https://wensity.com` | `https://ui.wensity.com/components` |
| `description` | Led on "AI interfaces" | Describes the catalog's actual breadth |

### Why

**URL.** The registry was first published from a personal account and has since moved to the Wensity organization at [wensity/registry](https://github.com/wensity/registry), which is now the canonical public host. The old repository remains published and unchanged, so anyone who hardcoded the previous raw URL in their own `components.json` keeps working.

The payloads at both locations are byte-identical (verified by SHA-256 on `registry.json` and item files), so resolution through the new URL returns exactly the same content. Verified with a clean project and no local `registries` config:

```
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wensity/registry/main/button.json
✔ Created 3 files
```

**Homepage.** `wensity.com` is the studio site. `ui.wensity.com/components` is the component catalog, which is what someone clicking through from the directory is looking for.

**Description.** The previous wording led with "AI interfaces", which is 4 of 70 items. The replacement describes the registry as it actually is: UI primitives, components, and motion, on Base UI and Tailwind CSS v4.

### Notes

- The registry remains free-only and MIT; Pro components are not published to it.
- Flat registry, no nested items, no `content` property in the index `files` array.
- `registry.json` and all 70 item payloads resolve over HTTPS.

pullRequests.author: rbadillap
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Adds a `base-color` migration that switches a project's base color and rewrites its theme CSS variables. It mirrors `migrate icons`, but for colors instead of icons.

```bash
# Migrate from the current base color in components.json.
npx shadcn@latest migrate base-color --to zinc

# Or pass both explicitly.
npx shadcn@latest migrate base-color --from zinc --to neutral --yes
```

Supported base colors: `neutral`, `zinc`, `stone`, `mauve`, `olive`, `mist`, `taupe`.

It rewrites the theme variables in the CSS file configured by `tailwind.css` and updates `baseColor` in `components.json`. Like `migrate icons`, it only touches tokens that still hold the source base color's value:

```
✔ Migration complete.
Updated baseColor in components.json to neutral.

Skipped 1 token. These were left untouched:
  - --primary: does not match the source base color
```

## Design decisions

- **Non-destructive by default.** Only tokens that still match the source base color are replaced; anything you customized is left untouched and reported at the end. Tokens identical across the two base colors (e.g. `radius`) are skipped silently.
- **`--from` defaults to the current `baseColor`**, so `--to` alone is the common path.
- **Delegates the write to `updateCssVars`** (the same updater `init`/`add` use). The only new logic is the value-provenance diff that decides which tokens are safe to overwrite.
- **Singular `base-color`** to match the `tailwind.baseColor` field (`icons` is plural because it swaps many icons; a project has one base color).
- Reuses the shared `-f, --from` / `-t, --to` flags, generalized to serve both migrations.

## How it maps to `migrate icons`

Same shape, different domain:

| | `migrate icons` | `migrate base-color` |
|---|---|---|
| Reference data (registry) | `icons/index.json` | `colors/{base}.json` |
| Source of truth for `from` | `iconLibrary` | `tailwind.baseColor` |
| Registry fetch | `getRegistryIcons()` | `getRegistryBaseColor()` |
| What it edits | UI components (`resolvedPaths.ui`) | the CSS file (`resolvedPaths.tailwindCss`) |
| Parser | ts-morph (imports + JSX) | postcss (`:root` / `.dark`) |
| Skip-and-report | no target equivalent / complex usage | token no longer matches source |
| Config write | `iconLibrary` | `tailwind.baseColor` |
| Pure, tested unit | `migrateIconsFileWithReport()` | `getBaseColorMigration()` |

## Tests

- Unit tests for `getBaseColorMigration`: replaces stock tokens, keeps and reports diverged tokens, ignores tokens unchanged across base colors, reports missing tokens, and handles v4 `hsl()` wrapping.
- Docs: adds a `migrate base-color` section to the CLI page.

pullRequests.body:
Stacked on #11501 — GitHub will retarget this to `main` once that merges.

Closes the gap called out in #11501: `shadcn add @pkg/item` (and `search`, `view`, `init`) now resolve registries declared in `package.json`, not just `components.json`.

## How it works

`ensureRegistriesInConfig` — the shared recovery path for missing registry namespaces — now checks `package.json` registries **before** falling back to the public registries index. Registries resolved from `package.json` are merged into the config in memory and are never persisted to `components.json`.

Two write-back paths were reworked to guarantee that:

- `ensureRegistriesInConfig` now builds its `components.json` update from the **file on disk** instead of the in-memory config, so in-memory registries (from `package.json`, or a previous call in the same run) can't leak into it. As a bonus, the write is now a minimal `registries`-only update instead of re-serializing the whole config.
- `init` now persists only registries discovered from the registries index, and overlays `package.json`-declared registries onto the install-time config in memory.

The function returns `discoveredRegistries` (index-found, persistable) and `packageJsonRegistries` (memory-only) separately so callers can make that distinction.

## Verification

- New unit tests for package.json resolution, index fallback, leak prevention, index-unavailable, and missing-file cases.
- Smoke-tested end to end: a project with `@pkg` declared only in `package.json` → `shadcn add @pkg/agent` installs the item from a local registry server and `components.json` is byte-identical afterwards.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Adds **SOCKS4/SOCKS5** support to the registry HTTP stack via `ALL_PROXY`, closing the most commonly requested gap in proxy coverage.

> **Scope note:** this PR originally replaced `node-fetch` with `undici` and expanded `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` handling. That portion shipped separately in #10905, and #11196 later added cross-origin redirect hardening. Per review feedback it has since been **rescoped again — PAC support has been removed and will land as a follow-up PR**, leaving SOCKS as the only new capability here. All redirect-security and error-enrichment logic from those PRs is preserved unchanged.

## Proxy capability matrix

| Capability | `main` today | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `HTTPS_PROXY` / `https_proxy` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `HTTP_PROXY` / `http_proxy` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy` bypass | ✅ | ✅ |
| HTTPS proxy (CONNECT tunneling) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Cross-origin redirect header stripping | ✅ | ✅ |
| SOCKS4 / SOCKS5 (`ALL_PROXY=socks*://…`) | ❌ | ✅ |
| PAC files (`PAC_URL=…`) | ❌ | ➡️ follow-up PR |

Part of the gap tracked in #5952.

## Architecture

`proxy.ts` keeps its existing `fetchWithProxy` entry point and manual-redirect logic exactly as-is. The only change to that layer is the dispatcher it hands to `fetch`: the module-level `EnvHttpProxyAgent` constant is replaced by a `createProxyDispatcher(env)` factory.

The factory is a **strict superset** of the previous behavior — it gates HTTP/HTTPS on the identical four env vars and returns the identical `EnvHttpProxyAgent`, then adds one higher-priority branch ahead of it:

```
        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
        │  createProxyDispatcher(env)  │
        └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                       │ examines env vars
             ┌─────────┼──────────────┬─────────────┐
             ▼         ▼              ▼             ▼
        ALL_PROXY=   HTTP_PROXY /   no proxy
        socks*?      HTTPS_PROXY?   env set
             │              │             │
             ▼              ▼             ▼
        socks Agent    EnvHttp-       undefined
        (custom        ProxyAgent     (global
        undici Agent   (unchanged)    dispatcher
        using socks                   used)
        package)
```

`ALL_PROXY` only activates the SOCKS branch for `socks*://` schemes (the curl convention); `ALL_PROXY=http://…` is intentionally left to the explicit `HTTP_PROXY` variable rather than being silently absorbed.

## What changed

### Code
- **`packages/shadcn/src/registry/proxy.ts`** — adds `createProxyDispatcher(env)`, the SOCKS `Agent` factory (a custom undici `Agent` whose `connect` is backed by the `socks` package), and the SOCKS URL parser. `fetchWithProxy` / `fetchOnce` / `getFailureReason` are untouched apart from the one-line dispatcher swap and one explanatory comment.

### Dependencies (`packages/shadcn/package.json`)
Adds `socks@^2.8.8` (~50 KB) and nothing else. `socks` was already present in the lockfile as a transitive dependency; promoting it to a direct dependency moves it `2.8.6 → 2.8.9`, which in turn updates its own `ip-address` dependency and drops two now-unused transitives. The lockfile diff is 32 lines and contains nothing else.

### Tests
- **`proxy.test.ts`** — 23 unit tests for `createProxyDispatcher` covering env-var detection (HTTP and SOCKS), priority ordering, and edge cases (empty values, malformed URLs, `ALL_PROXY` with a non-SOCKS scheme). The existing `fetchWithProxy` redirect tests are unchanged.
- **`proxy.integration.test.ts`** (new) — 10 integration tests against real local servers:
  - a CONNECT-tunneling HTTP proxy (verifies undici routes HTTPS via CONNECT)
  - a hand-rolled minimal SOCKS5 server (verifies SOCKS routing end to end, including that the SOCKS server observes a CONNECT to the correct origin host:port and that the HTTP proxy is not involved)

The CONNECT-tunnel test caught a real surprise during development: undici's `EnvHttpProxyAgent` always uses HTTP CONNECT even for `http://` targets, which a naive always-200 mock proxy would have hidden.

## Note for reviewers

`fetchOnce` must keep using the **global** `fetch` binding. `msw/node` patches `globalThis.fetch`, so importing `fetch` from `undici` there bypasses MSW's interceptor and breaks the registry tests — verified by a failed run during development. An inline comment documents this so future refactors don't regress it.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm test` — all **1711 tests across 83 files** in `packages/shadcn` pass
- [x] New proxy tests (33) cover env-var detection and end-to-end routing through HTTP and SOCKS
- [x] Existing MSW-backed registry tests (`fetcher.test.ts`, `api.test.ts`, `resolver.test.ts`) still pass — confirms MSW interception works through the new dispatcher
- [x] Existing `fetchWithProxy` redirect tests from #11196 still pass unchanged
- [x] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` validates cleanly against the regenerated lockfile

feat(shadcn): add SOCKS and PAC proxy support

Extends the registry's proxy capabilities beyond HTTP/HTTPS to cover
the standard proxy mechanisms users encounter:

- SOCKS4/SOCKS5 via ALL_PROXY=socks5://... (curl convention).
  Implementation uses the `socks` package wired into a custom undici

specificity of each mechanism (PAC can return mixed directives
per request; SOCKS and HTTP are per-process configurations).

- 7 new integration tests using a hand-rolled SOCKS5 server, a

Updates the data table documentation, demos, blocks, and the tasks example from TanStack Table v8 to **v9.0.0 stable** (released 2026-08-04). Supersedes #11055, redone from scratch on current main — now covering all three bases (`base`, `radix`, and the new `aria`).

This is deliberately a near 1:1 migration: update what's there, not a redesign.

## What changed

### Code (all three bases + new-york-v4)
- **Demos**: `examples/{aria,base,radix}/data-table-{demo,rtl}.tsx` and `registry/new-york-v4/examples/data-table-demo.tsx` migrated to the v9 API: a `tableFeatures()` declaration, `createColumnHelper()` column defs, and `useTable()` (row-model table options are gone — row models are registered on the features object).
- **dashboard-01 blocks** (×4): same migration; these tables deliberately register no faceting since they render no faceted UI ("include only what you use" is the point of v9's feature system).
- **Tasks example**: new shared `data-table-features.ts` module exports the `features` object and a `TasksTableFeatures` type, which the column defs and all reusable sub-components (`ReactTable<TasksTableFeatures, TData>`, `Column<...>`, `Row<...>`) share so the generics stay in sync.
- **Removed** the orphaned `components/cards/payments.tsx` — the live payments card was rewritten without TanStack Table a while back and nothing imports this copy.

### Docs
- `data-table.mdx` for **base, radix, and aria**: new "Set up Table Features" section, column-helper walkthrough, the v8 "add getPaginationRowModel" step replaced with "pagination is already enabled", a `flexRender` vs `<table.FlexRender />` callout, and all tanstack.com links updated to live v9 URLs (note: `…/latest/docs/introduction` 404s now; guides live under `…/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/*`). Line-highlight annotations recomputed for every changed code fence.
- `table.mdx` ×3: link updated to `tanstack.com/table/latest`.
- Fixed three pre-existing docs bugs while in there: base `data-table.mdx` previewed the **radix** demo (`styleName="radix-nova"`), radix `data-table.mdx` frontmatter said `base: base`, and the aria guide's basic-table snippet was missing `.map` on `getFlatHeaders()`.

### Registry / infra
- `@tanstack/react-table` bumped to `^9.0.0` in `apps/v4`. Registry item dependency strings stay bare — npm `latest` now resolves to v9.
- **Frozen v3 payloads**: `public/r/styles/{default,new-york}/dashboard-01.json` embed v8 code but declared a bare `@tanstack/react-table` dependency — since v9 became `latest`, legacy CLI installs would get v9 with v8 code. Pinned those two payloads to `@tanstack/react-table@^8.0.0` (one-line change each).
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: temporary `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` for the tanstack packages, since v9.0.0 is younger than the repo's 48h `minimumReleaseAge`. **Marked TODO — will be removed from this PR once the window passes (~Aug 6) before marking ready for review.**
